standard.title: Less common letter patterns
standard.description: use phoneme-grapheme (sound-letter) relationships and less common letter patterns to spell words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words with unpredictable sound-spelling relationships (AC9E2LY11). They have not yet focused specifically on less common patterns after short vowels and 3-letter blends.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use phoneme-grapheme relationships and less common letter patterns to spell words.

nodes.label: Less common patterns after short vowels
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and spell words with less common letter patterns after short vowels (e.g. 'tch', 'dge').
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly spell at least four words with less common patterns after short vowels (e.g. 'catch', 'bridge') and explain the pattern each uses.
nodes.typical_width: Use phonic knowledge to explore less common letter patterns after short vowels (e.g. 'tch', 'dge'); apply to spell words correctly in writing.
wider: Collect words with 'tch' and 'ch' after a short vowel and explore when each is used — developing a generalisation about the pattern
Find less common patterns in words from different curriculum areas and discuss how knowing the pattern helps spelling

response_modes.reason: Less common letter patterns are only identifiable through exposure to multiple examples. Students need to see enough instances of each pattern to recognise it reliably rather than treating each new word as unique.

success_criteria: Student correctly spells at least three words with a named less common pattern
Student can identify the pattern and explain why it appears at that position in the word

nodes.label: 3-letter blends
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read and write words with 3-letter consonant blends.
nodes.minimum_width: Read and write at least four words with 3-letter blends (e.g. 'str-', 'spr-', 'thr-') correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Use phonic knowledge and knowledge of letter patterns to spell words with 3-letter blends across reading and writing contexts.
wider: Collect a set of 3-letter blend words and sort by the blend at the start — discussing whether certain blends appear more in certain types of words
Apply 3-letter blend knowledge to read unfamiliar words encountered in subject-area texts

response_modes.reason: 3-letter blend reading and spelling develops through repeated practice with varied examples. Recognition becomes automatic through exposure rather than through more conceptual instruction.

success_criteria: Student correctly reads words with 3-letter blends without sounding out each letter separately
Student correctly spells words with 3-letter blends from memory or dictation
